newsitem.title: CHINA: Explosion in southwest China kills 21, injures 26.
newsitem.headline: Explosion in southwest China kills 21, injures 26.

text.p: An explosion at a private store for materials used in firework production in southwestern China has killed 21 people and injured 26, including three seriously, officials and state media said.
The huge blast occurred on February 4 in a private home in a residential area of Xichong in southwestern Sichuan province, said a local official contacted by telephone on Wednesday.

The official said it was not yet clear what had caused the blast, but a report in the Yangcheng Evening News said it appeared that three tonnes of materials used to make fireworks had suddenly detonated.
The bodies of some of those in the blast had been blown to the other side of a river near the house, the newspaper said in an edition seen in Beijing on Wednesday.

More than 20 homes were levelled by the explosion and 20 bodies were recovered from the rubble, it said. One person was dead on arrival in hospital and 26 were injured, three of whom were in a serious condition.
Chinese traditionally set off firecrackers to celebrate the lunar new year, which this year fell on February 7, and each year many people die in explosions at underground plants making fireworks.
